milestones.name: Other modules read the one sky and Sun, and one cloud optical depth dims direct sunlight once

items.statement: Each frame every scene contribution is lent one environment identity: source epoch and simulation time, and the true Sun (geometric direction, raw perpendicular illuminance, colour, angular radius, no attenuation applied) kept apart from the apparent surface light. The epoch changes when the sky model, the air profile or a LUT generation (a replacement of resources or model) changes, and never when only time advances and chart contents are recomputed.
items.ask: Do tests in ./dev check cover an epoch change on profile change and on device replacement, no change across a time scrub, and the true Sun staying continuous through sunset while the apparent surface light fades? Is the identity produced in one place and only read elsewhere?

items.statement: Through the lent bind-group layout and WGSL library alone, a contribution's own pipeline evaluates the five lent operations on Metal: Sun light at a world position, sky radiance along a direction, incident diffuse, aerial (T,S) from the camera to a point, and environment reflection with its split-sum pair. Each meets its handoff row H1-H5 in the design's numerical acceptance table, and the wrong lookups that H2 and H4 name fail.
items.ask: Read the referee tests. Does the contribution use only the lent layout and library, with no private chart, mip or storage-gain knowledge? Does each of H1-H5 assert the bound its row names against the reference its row names, and never against the forward pass's own output? For H2 and H4, is the expected value an f64 filtered decode written apart from the library's code, on the live product and on the known field, and does the test fail if a single-texel or single-slice lookup passes? Is their allowance the design's C/32 + 1e-5 M + Q, with Q one stored half-float step and nothing wider, on a known field whose neighbouring texels differ by at least 32 stored steps? Is one case of each row repeated at a non-unit exposure scale? Does H5 vary direction, roughness, the raw Sun's illuminance, the night term and a rewritten sky? Are the preserved referees P1-P11 unchanged in reference, cases and bound?

A registered provider's optical depth multiplies direct sunlight by exp(-tau), read for the receiver's own world point, exactly once on every direct-Sun receiver (terrain, synthetic instances, cooked meshes and each lit march sample of the cooked volume) and changes nothing else: sky light, emission and geometric shadow are unchanged, the factor is exactly 1 outside the field's declared support, and toggling the provider resets only the history it must.

items.statement: Near the ground a read of the lent aerial `(T,S)` is what the point's own line holds. In the cases of the design's `Numerical acceptance for the air at the ground`, at all eight camera pitches, the read at a point between two rows of the volume matches the product's own column along that point's line: transmittance within 0.01 × expected + 0.001, solar in-scatter within 0.025 × expected + 0.0025 × that column's in-scatter at 32 km, each plus one stored step, and the night term within 10%. The same reads with every column held at its value where it met the ground miss that allowance by more than five times, at one pitch or more, for the points 30 km away above the horizon and the ground points 10 km away. The worst share of the allowance by Sun and channel is on record, with the same reads at a Sun 0.5° up dead ahead and at a 90° field of view beside it; the record decides nothing.

Under the ground, does the pass follow the density law below zero altitude and dim the Sun's light with depth, and not hold the surface's air or its light?

items.statement: Nothing above the ground moved. For frames recorded at the commit this milestone started from, every texel of a line that never meets the ground, and every layer that ends before its line meets the ground, holds the bytes that commit stored. Past the ground every stored value is finite, and each layer's stored transmittance lies between 0 and 1 and is no higher than the layer's before it. Two layers may store the same transmittance, zero included, because half-float storage rounds a value that is still falling to the same step. On a line with two or more layers past the ground, the last layer's stored transmittance is lower than that of the first layer past the ground.

items.statement: The air's aerosol is an input of the air profile in two numbers: its amount, as the extinction at 550 nm, and its kind, as an Ångström exponent from 0 to 2. At the defaults, today's amount and an exponent of 0, every chart holds the bytes it held before. At another amount the lent Sun light and the transmittance chart change with it, and at an exponent of 1.3 the bands take different aerosol, so a profile that gives every band the 550 nm aerosol fails the test. The charts follow a change of either number within the lag the profile declares, and a change of either does not move the environment epoch.
items.ask: Did any existing reference, case, bound or test in the numerical acceptance table change? None may: the defaults draw as before.

items.statement: Inside the view volume the air's solar in-scatter is shadowed once. Behind an occluder that the shadow cascades hold, a cell takes no single-scattered sunlight; under a registered Sun-path optical depth a cell takes the cloud factor at its own position; and a registered haze scale is not applied as well. Transmittance and the night term are unchanged by either.
items.ask: Does the test show that the forward decoder's own split of solar in-scatter by a surface's shadow is not applied on top of the volume's, by comparing a shadowed surface's aerial term with the volume's value at its depth?

items.statement: A ray that leaves the volume takes the volume's terminal pair once: its sky pixel is `R·L + ΔS`, with `L` the clear sky's radiance there and `(R, ΔS)` the pair the volume itself reports for that ray. With no provider `R` is exactly 1. Where nothing shadows a ray's air, `ΔS` is exactly 0 and the pixel is the clear sky's to the bit. On a ray whose near air a cascade occluder shadows, and on one the registered Sun-path optical depth shadows, `ΔS` is negative and the pixel equals `L + ΔS` at a tolerance the test states. On each of those two rays a sky that takes `ΔS` twice, and a sky left as the clear sky, miss that tolerance: the test runs both through the same comparison and each fails.
items.ask: Does the test take `L` from the clear sky and `(R, ΔS)` from the volume's own output for the same ray, and neither from the composed pixel? Does it run a sky that takes `ΔS` twice and a sky left as the clear sky through the same comparison on both shadowed rays, and does each fail there?

items.statement: The view volume integrates a provider's medium coefficients with the air, each counted once. For a uniform slab of known extinction, solar kernel and ambient source standing in the air inside the provider's ramp, at visual ranges of 30 m, 150 m and 2 km, the lent transmittance to a point beyond the slab is the air's times the slab's, at a tolerance the test states, with the grid's slices as they are and with twice as many, and a slab in sunlight adds light on the ray. A volume that applies the slab twice, or the air twice, fails the test.
items.ask: Does the test show both wrong compositions fail, and is the coefficients' sum with the air's taken before integration, not after?

items.statement: A ray that leaves the volume composes once. Through a slab near the camera a sky pixel is `R·L + ΔS`, and a star drawn over it adds `R` times its own light and no second `ΔS`: a pixel that holds sky and a star equals the reference for their sum, and the Sun's disc dims by `R`. With a provider registered and its coefficients zero, sky pixels hold the same bytes as with none.
items.ask: Does the tested pixel hold both sky and a star with the slab's `ΔS` at least a tenth of their sum, so that correcting each draw by itself fails? Does the far aerial operation beyond 32 km, if `CLOUDS` has built it, compose the same terminal pair, and does the test say whether it was present?

items.statement: The Sun-path optical depth has a ground band that holds the whole path to the Sun. With one registered, the factor on terrain, synthetic instances, cooked meshes, each lit sample of the cooked volume and the incident-light meter is the exponential of minus one read: the band at the receiver's own position for a receiver inside it, and the 2D field at or above the band's top and outside its region. The two are never added. A receiver in the band under an upper cloud of optical depth ln 2, with no condensate near it, takes 0.5, and condensate near it adds its own path alone. The factor is continuous across the band's top and across its border. With none registered the shaders are composed without the read, as before.
